Title: Last registration step asks for the mobile number and sends the user back to step 2
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Register as a seeker through to the final step 2) Refresh, or return to the tab later 3) Observe
Expected: Registration progress survives a page reload
Actual: The user is bounced back to the phone step and must start again
Root Cause / Fix: CONFIRMED: the verify-email guard router.replace('/register/phone') fires when the in-memory context is empty. Registration state is deliberately React context, never localStorage, so a plaintext password is never persisted - hence any refresh restarts the flow. Fix (in the rework): persist only NON-SECRET progress (phone, email, verified flags, step) to sessionStorage; the password stays in memory only.  >> FIXED in f18590c. Non-secret progress (phone, email, verified flags, step) mirrors to sessionStorage behind an explicit allowlist; the PASSWORD is never persisted, nor are File handles or dev OTP echoes. Guards wait for hydration - persistence alone would not have fixed the bounce.

Confirmed against the served markup. The role is now set from an effect once the destination is known. Footer.tsx deliberately unchanged - inferring from the validated returnUrl fixes EVERY employer deep link, not just the three footer ones.

Title: Registration collects date of birth and gender but never sends them - no minimum age is enforced anywhere
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Register as a seeker 2) Enter a date of birth under 18 3) Complete registration
Expected: Registration is refused - the product requires 18+
Actual: The account is created. The BE age >= 18 check never ran because dateOfBirth and gender were never in the register payload
Root Cause / Fix: FIXED in 206b065. api.ts omitted both fields and carried a stale comment claiming the BE had no field for them; it has accepted both since BR-3, and dateOfBirthSchema is where the age rule lives. Verified live: born 2010-01-01 -> 400 {path: dateOfBirth}; born 2000-05-15 -> 201 with both persisted; gender 'male' -> 400. Age is now also checked on the PROFILE step, because the server rejection otherwise lands on the password screen six steps later with no date field on it. NOTE: mobile always sent both - this was portal-only.

Title: /api/otp/send reveals whether a phone number is already registered
Steps to Reproduce: 1) POST /api/otp/send with a registered number 2) Repeat with an unregistered one 3) Compare
Expected: Responses do not disclose whether an account exists
Actual: A registered number returns 400 'This phone number is already registered'; an unregistered one succeeds - a phone-enumeration oracle
Status: Open - DECISION required, not a defect fix
Root Cause / Fix: Pre-existing BE behaviour, not introduced by the auth rework. It is also exactly what makes the error actionable: a returning user is told to sign in instead of being sent to re-verify a phone that already has an account. Keeping it trades a privacy leak for usability; closing it means a generic message and a worse dead end. Asrar's call - BE change either way.
